assessment.summary: A recurrent biological threat whose severe-pandemic form could greatly exceed the already-large annual burden of seasonal influenza; the main watch item is H5N1, which kills roughly half of the people it is confirmed to infect but has not acquired sustained human-to-human transmission.
assessment.timeframe: Pandemics recur on the order of every few decades; timing is not predictable.

claims.text: The WHO states seasonal influenza causes 290,000 to 650,000 respiratory deaths annually.
The WHO states there are around a billion cases of seasonal influenza annually worldwide, including 3-5 million cases of severe illness.

WHO's cumulative table of confirmed human cases of avian influenza A(H5N1) reported to WHO for 2003-2026 records 1,002 cases and 479 deaths across 25 reporting countries, with data in WHO headquarters as of 7 August 2026.

WHO states the World Health Assembly adopted the WHO Pandemic Agreement in May 2025, and that at the close of the seventh meeting of the Intergovernmental Working Group on 17 July 2026 member states were still negotiating the agreement's Pathogen Access and Benefit Sharing annex, with an eighth meeting scheduled for 14-18 September 2026.

description: A novel influenza strain to which the population has little immunity could spread worldwide and cause mortality far exceeding ordinary seasonal influenza, as in 1918. Pandemics have recurred several times per century, and the ordinary seasonal burden — around a billion cases and 290,000 to 650,000 respiratory deaths a year — is the floor a pandemic strain would build on. Highly pathogenic avian influenza A(H5N1) remains the most closely watched candidate: WHO has logged just over a thousand confirmed human infections since 2003, almost half of them fatal, but these are sporadic cases tied to animal exposure rather than sustained human-to-human transmission. The international response framework is still being completed — the WHO Pandemic Agreement was adopted in May 2025, but its Pathogen Access and Benefit Sharing annex, which would govern how samples and countermeasures are shared during a pandemic, is still under negotiation.
name: Influenza Pandemic
